title: collab P4: inbound asset sync has no size cap and no content-hash verification (DoS + integrity)
description:
Adversarial QA of task 1347 (collab P4, commit 884649b: share dialog + out-of-band asset sync). The new peer-to-peer asset channel that transfers bitmap/sound/video BYTES out-of-band (kept out of the CRDT, only an asset-hash:<sha256> ref travels in the Y.Doc) accepts inbound RESPONSE frames from any joined peer with NEITHER a size cap NOR a content-hash check. P4 wired the share dialog (CollabControls/ShareDialog), so a real malicious peer with the share link can now reach this surface end-to-end.

TWO COUPLED GAPS, both in packages/authoring-ui/src/collab.

(1) NO SIZE CAP -> OOM/DoS. assetChannel.ts AssetSyncEngine.handle() decodes a RESPONSE and calls this.store.put(msg.hash, msg.bytes.slice(), msg.mime). The RESPONSE framing (assetChannel.ts decode) reads bytes = frame.subarray(o) — the ENTIRE remainder of the frame, unbounded. The webrtc transport (webrtcAssetTransport.ts, single data-channel message) hands the whole buffer through. There is no max-asset-size constant anywhere. A peer can broadcast (or answer a request with) a multi-hundred-MB / GB RESPONSE -> .slice() allocates a full copy -> OOM / tab crash for every peer that receives it. assetSync.ts then re-internalizes and base64-encodes the bytes into a data URI (another large allocation) on resolution. No back-pressure, no per-peer rate limit, no cap.

(2) NO CONTENT-HASH VERIFICATION -> integrity break + crafted-decode vector. The store is CONTENT-ADDRESSED: the Y.Doc references a library item by asset-hash:<sha256> and the bytes are supposed to be the bytes whose sha256 == that hash. But handle() stores msg.bytes under msg.hash WITHOUT recomputing sha256Hex(msg.bytes) === msg.hash (AssetStore.put also does no verification — assetStore.ts:53, first-writer-wins by key). So a malicious peer answering a request for hash X with ARBITRARY bytes (or a crafted/malformed image) poisons the store: internalizeAssets (assetExternalize.ts:115) then does bytesToDataUri(stored.bytes, stored.mime) and injects the attacker-controlled bytes as the dataUri of the victim's legit library item, which the renderer/compiler then decodes. This defeats the content-addressing integrity guarantee and is a crafted-decode (image-decoder) attack vector. mime is also taken verbatim from the peer (no type validation). First-writer-wins means a fast malicious answer can beat an honest holder.

WHY REACHABLE NOW (1347/P4). Pre-P4 collab was library-only / not user-reachable. P4 mints the share link in the Share dialog and a joiner connects via join(link) -> joinCollab -> webrtcAssetTransport over the y-webrtc mesh. internalizeAssets issues engine.requestMany(missing) for any referenced-but-missing hash on every inbound apply; any peer in the room answers. So a joined peer (who has the link/k) can both DoS via oversized RESPONSE and poison assets via wrong-bytes RESPONSE.

TRANSPORT/E2E NOTE (not a leak, but an asymmetry worth recording): the DOC and AWARENESS ride y-webrtc's password-derived AES-GCM E2E layer; ASSET frames bypass it (own MAGIC prefix + raw simple-peer peer.send) and rely only on DTLS. No server/relay sees the bytes (direct P2P) so there is no clear-text-via-signaling leak, but assets are NOT under the room-password E2E layer the doc is. Acceptable but should be documented in docs/37.

FIX DIRECTION (collab-package / authoring-ui only; do NOT change core importer/renderer semantics):
- Add a MAX_ASSET_BYTES cap. Reject/ignore a RESPONSE whose bytes exceed it (and ideally bound the frame before .slice()). Pick a generous-but-finite limit (authoring bitmaps/sounds) and document it; chunked transfer + back-pressure is a separate follow-up already noted in webrtcAssetTransport.ts.
- VERIFY the content hash before put: in AssetSyncEngine.handle() (or AssetStore.put), compute sha256Hex(bytes) (already exported from @flash/core fla/asset-hash.ts; the canonical hash is sha256 of the decoded bytes per hashDataUri) and DROP the response if it does not equal the requested hash. This makes a poisoned-bytes answer a no-op and preserves content-addressing. Optionally validate mime against a small allowlist.
- Re-run the 2-peer asset test (assetSync2peer.test.ts) plus new adversarial cases: oversized RESPONSE is dropped without OOM; wrong-bytes RESPONSE for a hash is rejected and the honest holder's bytes still resolve.

ACCEPTANCE: an inbound RESPONSE larger than the cap is dropped (no unbounded allocation); an inbound RESPONSE whose sha256(bytes) != hash is dropped (store never poisoned, placeholder stays until correct bytes arrive); existing collab tests (authoring-ui 1127, collab P0 22) stay green; solo unaffected.

Found during read-only adversarial QA of 1347 at HEAD f32d90f. No product code changed by the QA pass. Related: 1351 (rebuildDoc/cloneJson DoS) is the doc-side peer-reachable DoS; this is the asset-side one — both are now reachable because P4 wired the share link.
